title: ops quiet-window communication scratch
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the "quiet window" ops communication. Not final — meant to capture the message, Q&A, and handoff checklist so we can push a short Slack + internal email and a blurb for the all-hands.

Context:
- We anticipate a higher-than-normal resource contention this weekend due to partner cluster maintenance (region eu-west-2).
- Goal: reduce pager noise, keep customer impacts minimal, surface fallback routing, and set clear expectations for non-critical experiments and non-urgent pushes.
- This is NOT a customer-facing outage notice; it's internal prep + internal comms for teams.

Quick TL;DR (for Slack):
- Title: Ops: Quiet Window (EU-West-2) — limited non-essential work this weekend
- One-liner: We expect reduced spare capacity in eu-west-2 from Sat 03/14 00:00 UTC to Sun 03/15 23:59 UTC. Please avoid non-urgent deploys and heavy load tests. SRE will triage active SLO-impacting alerts.
- Link: (internal playbook) CONFLUENCE-1234

Draft Slack message (internal #ops-alerts / #eng-all):
"Hi all — heads up: partner maintenance in eu-west-2 will likely reduce spare GPU capacity this weekend (Sat 03/14 -> Sun 03/15). Please pause non-essential experiments, scheduled large-batch embeddings, and non-urgent infra changes. SRE will monitor and run fallback routing to other regions if needed. If you have a customer-facing launch scheduled this weekend, reply here ASAP so we can coordinate. More details in CONFLUENCE-1234."

All-hands quick bullet for Q&A slide (3 lines max):
- What: temporary reduced capacity in eu-west-2 for ~48hrs.
- Why: partner infra maintenance + expected burst from partner migrations.
- What we’ll do: automatic routing to compatible regions, temporary throttle policies, prioritized remediation if SLOs degrade.

Talking points for EMs / team leads (to use in syncs):
- Reassure teams: normal traffic routing remains; we will only throttle/route if latency or error budgets are at risk.
- Ask teams: postpone noncritical experiments & non-timeboxed load tests. If launch is critical, escalate to me + Arun immediately so we can request reserved burst or prioritize capacity.
- Remind: Observability dashboards show per-route token latency & cost — check the "eu-west-2" panel and the routing fallback metric.

Q&A (predicted) + suggested answers:
Q: Will customers notice increased latency?
A: Possibly for some long-tail routes pinned to eu-west-2. SRE will route to compatible model variants/regions; most traffic will be seamless. If an SLO is breached we will notify affected PMs and trigger a rollback/fallback.

Q: Can we spin up Dedicated capacity for a hotfix?
A: For urgent, customer-impacting fixes we can request a temporary dedicated slot — contact Arun and I with justification (customer, expected TPS). We will evaluate and escalate.

Q: What counts as "non-essential"?
A: Load tests, large embedding batches (>100k requests), scheduled infra migrations, non-blocking model eval runs. Anything customer-facing with committed timelines counts as essential — tag it in-channel.

Ops checklist (what SRE/Oncall does):
- Pre-weekend: ensure runbook updated (CONFLUENCE-1234).
- 6 hours before window: post Slack notice and email to product leads.
- During window: monitor key SLOs (latency P95, error rate per-route), watch fallback routing success rate, run manual failover if automated routing fails.
- Post-window: run short retro, capture incidents, publish short summary.

Escalation contacts (order):
- Oncall SRE: Ben Cho (primary) — pager ON
- Ops lead: Carmen Liu (this doc owner) — slack/phone
- Infra eng: Arun Patel — for capacity requests
- Product/regional PM: Sofia Martinez — customer impact comms

Message variations (for managers to copy/paste):
- Short: "Please avoid non-urgent deploys and heavy experiments in eu-west-2 this weekend (03/14-03/15). SRE will triage any issues. Link: CONFLUENCE-1234"
- Slightly longer (for email): see TL;DR + list of examples of non-essential work.

Customer-facing opt-in notice (draft) — only if we need to notify customers who have reserved eu-west-2 capacity:
"We are performing partner-coordinated maintenance in eu-west-2 that may temporarily reduce available spare capacity between 03/14 00:00 UTC and 03/15 23:59 UTC. We will route workloads to other compatible regions where possible. If you require guaranteed capacity during this window, reply to this thread and we will prioritize your workloads. We apologize for any inconvenience."

Risk notes / gotchas (personal):
- Some internal routes are hard-pinned to eu-west-2 for data locality — these will see the most impact. Need to surface list to product owners.
- Automated fallback to other regions may increase cost; budget owners should be notified if we expect >10% cross-region routing.
- Watch alert storm risk — many teams may trigger small alerts that together seem noisy; consider a short suppression window for low-priority alerts.

TODOs (next steps, quick):
- [ ] Finalize Slack + email copy (this doc -> publish) — Carmen
- [ ] Confirm list of pinned routes (ask network team) — Arun
- [ ] Prepare brief for Friday all-hands slide (2 bullets) — Sofia
- [ ] Update runbook with explicit fallback thresholds — Ben

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep comms lean — too many details will cause ticket flood.
- If SLOs degrade, we must have a one-paragraph customer message ready.
- Follow up with billing if cross-region routing causes >15% variance in cost for any major customer.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after quick sync with Arun & Ben (T+2h).
